title: U.S. House · Washington's 2nd District
area: Northwest Washington, including Whatcom, Skagit, Island and San Juan counties, and part of Snohomish County.

context.text: Rick Larsen and Edwin Feller advanced from the August 4, 2026 top-two primary, defeating two other Democratic candidates. Larsen won the primary with 44.9% of the vote to Feller's 32.9%.

candidates.name: Rick Larsen
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 4 top-two primary with 44.9% of the vote

summary.text: Rick Larsen is the Democratic incumbent U.S. Representative for Washington's 2nd District, which he has represented since 2001. Before Congress he worked in public affairs for the Washington State Dental Association, in economic development at the Port of Everett, and on the Snohomish County Council. He is the ranking Democrat on the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee and says his 2026 campaign centers on affordability, transportation, veterans, the fentanyl crisis, and the environment.

background.text: Born in 1965 and raised in Arlington, Washington, where he attended public schools.
Earned a bachelor's degree from Pacific Lutheran University in 1983 and a master's degree in public affairs from the University of Minnesota in 1990.
Worked as director of public affairs for the Washington State Dental Association and then as an economic development official with the Port of Everett.
Served on the Snohomish County Council before running for Congress; Wikipedia lists his service as January 1998 to January 2001.
Won election to the U.S. House on November 7, 2000, defeating Republican John Koster and two minor-party candidates, and has been re-elected to 12 further terms.

Served as the lead Democrat (ranking member) on the Transportation and Infrastructure Committee's Aviation Subcommittee from 2013 to 2022, and was elected by House Democrats as ranking member of the full committee for the 118th Congress, a post he still holds.

His 2025-2026 committee assignments are the Transportation and Infrastructure Committee and its Aviation, Coast Guard and Maritime Transportation, Highways and Transit, Water Resources and Environment, and other subcommittees.

Other roles listed on his official site include member of the NATO Parliamentary Assembly, co-chair of the bipartisan U.S.-China Working Group, co-chair of the Congressional Arctic Working Group and Congressional Austria Caucus, and member of the New Democrat Coalition and its Trade Task Force.
According to his official biography, he lives in Everett with his spouse, Tiia Karlén; they have two sons.

record.text: Sits on the House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure for the 2025-2026 Congress, including the Aviation, Coast Guard and Maritime Transportation, Highways and Transit, and Water Resources and Environment subcommittees.

candidates.name: Edwin Feller
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the August 4 top-two primary with 32.9% of the vote

summary.text: Edwin Feller is the Republican candidate for Washington's 2nd District, an 83-year-old retired HVAC tradesman and business owner from Lynden who has not previously run for office. He is the only Republican who ran in the 2026 race and advanced from the August 4 top-two primary with 32.9% of the vote. His campaign website lists priorities on public safety, energy permitting, women's sports, medical procedures for minors, and immigration.

background.text: Born on his family's Hampton Road farm in Lynden, Washington, and graduated from Lynden Christian High School in 1960.
Spent about 60 years in the HVAC industry. He founded Feller Heating, spent about 18 years in a union sheet metal job, and has owned three businesses, according to Cascadia Daily News.
Spent much of his career overseas in construction trades work for contractors of the U.S. government, including several years of HVAC work for the U.S. State Department at facilities in 60 countries.
Is a first-time candidate for public office; he told the Lynden Tribune he decided to run because "somebody needs to run against Rick."

priorities.text: Feller's campaign platform calls for a federal "Safe Streets" mandate tying grants to local cooperation, designating cartels as foreign terrorist organizations, and ending sanctuary policies.
Calls for dismantling current environmental mandates, streamlining energy permits, expanding nuclear and hydroelectric capacity, and repealing federal carbon taxes.
priorities.quote: Dismantling radical environmental mandates, streamlining energy permits, expanding nuclear and hydroelectric capacity, and repealing federal carbon taxes to deliver affordable, reliable American-made energy.

positions.summary: Supports a federal Safe Streets mandate tying grants to local cooperation with immigration enforcement and ending sanctuary policies.
Campaign platform calls for repealing federal carbon taxes, dismantling current environmental mandates, and expanding nuclear and hydroelectric energy capacity.
